Epilepsy clinic letter
Consultation: 05 March 2025
Patient: Laura Chen, aged 28

Dear colleague,

Laura attended our clinic following referral for episodic paroxysmal sensory symptoms.

She describes episodes of sudden visual scintillations followed by dizziness and paresthesia in the left hand lasting 10 to 15 minutes, occurring roughly weekly, with the latest episode on 28 February 2025. Her clinical assessment is challenging. The differential diagnosis includes focal sensory epilepsy, migraine aura without headache, or vestibular events. I cannot establish a definitive diagnosis of epilepsy today, and the clinical picture remains indeterminate. She takes no anti-seizure medications.

We arranged brain MRI and routine outpatient EEG. Follow-up in four months.

Laura says she has never lost awareness during her sensory episodes. Her mother reports that Laura did not respond to her voice during the episode on 28 February and believes awareness was lost. Laura disputes this account. I have not resolved this reporter disagreement; neither report settles the epilepsy versus migraine differential.

Epilepsy clinic letter
Consultation: 16 July 2025
Patient: Laura Chen

Dear colleague,

I reviewed Laura today. Her brain MRI was completely normal.

She continues to experience weekly sensory episodes, with the latest on 10 July 2025. Routine EEG showed non-specific theta slowing without epileptiform discharges. Having reviewed detailed symptom logs, focal aware sensory seizures remain a leading possibility, but migraine aura without headache remains an equally plausible differential. The diagnostic categorization remains uncertain and unresolved.

No anti-seizure medication commenced. We agreed to arrange prolonged ambulatory EEG monitoring. Follow-up in four months.
